`test_api` now imports `pandas.api.internals` itself before checking `dir(pd.api)`, so it no longer depends on another test having imported it first. I haven't run it, since I can't run anything here.

The change is in `pandas/tests/api/test_api.py`: one `importlib.import_module("pandas.api.internals")` call at the top of `test_api`, with a comment explaining why.

I chose this over importing `internals` in `pandas/api/__init__.py`. `pandas/api/internals.py` does `from pandas import DataFrame, Index`, so importing it during `import pandas` could cause a circular import. The module also seems intentionally not auto-imported: another check in the same test file (line 529) explicitly skips `internals`. Whether `pd.api.internals` should be reachable from a bare `import pandas` is still your call. If you want that, it would be a separate change.
